title: [E2-3] 브라우저 API와 인증
goal: Verify the existing E2-3 implementation against its complete approved contract, reusing the real synthetic integration bridge instead of rebuilding auth or a client. Expose exact source defects and ownership gaps before any product-source repair. This assignment does not grant source ownership or Done authority.

readiness.priorCompletion: CCC-204 is Done for E2-2 only; its final synthetic natural-registration proof is not E2-3 or hosted Supabase certification.

acceptance: Inventory the approved 21 error codes and map them to the actual Browser transport and consumer behavior. Map every required code; report additions, missing codes or changed semantics explicitly rather than truncating to 21 or inventing an oracle.

Trace canonical DTOs and actual decoders across browser API boundaries. Exercise meaningful valid, nullable/optional, malformed and unauthorized/error responses through real consumer code, with deterministic synthetic inputs and actual error behavior.

Exercise actual Browser transport behavior, authenticated requests, cancellation/stale-session handling, and error/revocation/logout boundaries required by S2 and existing E2-3 contracts. Distinguish client protocol behavior with a synthetic issuer from hosted provider guarantees.
Verify token and PII storage boundaries in the real browser, including the relevant lifecycle transitions. Never serialize credentials or sensitive page/cache bodies into evidence.

Verify signed bootstrap/installation allowlisting and actual URL/origin rejection through unchanged validators and consumers. Preserve independent API/Auth binding and the approved optional Cloud MFA policy.

Verify Electron same-origin/protocol/navigation contract with the actual available Electron runtime or existing real-runtime harness. A Chrome mock of Electron or a source-string check is not runtime proof. If unavailable, report exact missing capability and finish other reachable criteria.

Evaluate actual applicable response-header/CSP/CORS implementation, not the fixture's hand-authored headers. In particular, the CCC-204 fixture needed apiBase plus a trailing slash for descendant API requests. Determine what the actual runtime emits and whether it matches the intended S2 contract; do not silently relax production policy.

executionRules: Verify actual own pane/session/cwd/branch. Only controller w1N:p6 assigns work, changes ticket status or resets sessions. Do not read full old orchestration history or private session files.

Inspect the exact current contracts and build a finite acceptance matrix before runtime work. Work from a commit-pinned disposable snapshot; prove imports resolve to that snapshot and original worktree/WIP remain unchanged.

Reuse installed dependencies and prior fixture construction. Copy or adapt only the minimal test glue inside the new owned evidence directory so running it never overwrites the immutable CCC-204 artifacts. No new packages, worktrees, agents or application scaffold.

Test-only fixture extensions needed to exercise E2-3 are permitted, but they must drive actual validators/handlers/consumers. Malformed error/DTO test inputs are valid boundary tests; arbitrary successful authentication, React/session injection and fixed /me success are not.

Keep keys/passwords/tokens memory-only, use only synthetic users/data, and allow only fixture-local network and runtime writes. Fixture-specific TLS trust may be reused; broad TLS-ignore flags, global trust/DNS changes, credential discovery and real external providers are forbidden. Do not capture credential/OTP/QR screens or raw auth/body/HAR dumps.

Use actual existing targeted contract/security commands where suitable, once after fixture/source freeze. Preserve tests and assertions; report name-filtered exclusions precisely. Do not rerun unrelated CCC-201/CCC-204/CCC-286 or project-wide suites.

Services must use hub start with readiness evidence. Browser scenarios must use the real surface and default page execution context where service-worker observations require it. Do not add placeholders to satisfy a test.

A source defect does not grant source ownership. Report exact path, violated contract, actual reproduction, existing owner and minimal repair packet. Do not fix apps/client, apps/web, adapters, packages, shared UI/CSS/design guards, auth policy, schema or migrations here.

Do not demand production access just because a provider is synthetic; separate independently testable protocol/validation behavior from real-hosted/OS guarantees. If a required real capability is absent, record that criterion blocked with concrete evidence, then finish other independent reachable criteria without repeating the same failure indefinitely.

Stop only owned runtime, collect all results, write the contracted JSON, end the turn and remain idle. The existing completion monitor notifies controller once. No Linear/control-state writes, other-pane prompts, /new, commits, pushes, deployments or second ticket.
